claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation a bit better.

Could you tell me why Alex lives elsewhere? For example:
- Is he living with another family member or someone else?
- Is he in local authority care?
- Is he in hospital?
- Or is there another arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question about Alex's situation:

Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or does he spend 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 or more days in a row) at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home that regularly. He stays at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more question: You mentioned Alex has been in local authority care for a few months. Has he been in care for more than 8 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been about 3 months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 3 months, which is longer than the 8-week threshold.
- After 8 weeks in care, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit unless certain exceptions apply.
- The main exception is if Alex spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or spends 2 consecutive nights each week (or 7 or more consecutive days) at home. Since Alex stays at the care home full-time and doesn't come home regularly, this exception doesn't apply.

**If your circumstances change** – for example, if Alex starts spending 2 nights in a row each week at home, or 7 or more consecutive days at home – you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to contact HMRC to discuss your situation.

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help you with?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and has been in local authority care for approximately 3 months (more than 8 weeks). According to the rules for Child Benefit when a child is in care, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit after 8 weeks. There is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, or spends 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 or more days in a row at home. However, Alex stays at the care home full-time and does not come home regularly enough to meet any of these exceptions. Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
